purpose: Editor consumers of recovered game functions. Matching status comes from Decomp, not this list. Symbols are case-insensitive; ROM offsets in source comments are US Rev 0 z64 offsets.

groups.behavior: Independent scenario squad member construction
groups.benefit: Scenario squads can have five independently configured members while retaining the original constructor and its allocation/finalization path.
groups.preserve: Original pool selection, class-copy behavior, level initialization, equipment precedence, leader flags and special naming. Soldier groups retain the original cohort path. The imported original source remains unchanged in the accepted library.

groups.behavior: Combat animation directory and instruction lookup
groups.benefit: PC pose decoding and the ROM class reader now share accepted operand behavior; track future upstream changes.
groups.preserve: All five functions are retained unchanged in accepted/combat_pose_metadata.c. PC decoding is a bounded linear bulk walk with cached playback. Keep private registration and wide frames/states. The generic directory getter remains host-owned; the two empty helpers are source companions, not missing features.

groups.behavior: Class/action/mode animation selection and fallback
groups.benefit: The guided Combat animation preview uses a bounded C adaptation of the accepted selector underneath existing overrides.
groups.preserve: Expanded classes, full-byte class-copy comparison, missing-source-group fallback, default selector 40, all three modes and OBSO override precedence.

groups.behavior: Actor pose execution and frame timing
groups.benefit: Replace reconstructed pose dispatch with recovered control flow when matching C becomes available.
groups.preserve: Bounded/resumable preview execution, shared callbacks and private or wide-frame extensions.

groups.behavior: Ordinary and combat-body actor initialization
groups.benefit: Improve initialization of scene actors, linked equipment bodies and their initial poses.
groups.preserve: Current source/owner distinctions, linked-body policy and host resource ownership. Existing code implements record-boundary portions, not every original service.

groups.behavior: Dynamic cutscene cast selection from the player's army
groups.benefit: Keep roster selection, equivalent appearances and leader fallback aligned with recovered behavior, including dynamic scenes such as 01FA8BF4.
groups.preserve: 002ABB3C already has a host adaptation; the predicates are reconstructed. Story-script cast choices are separate data/logic and are not automatically replaced by a roster function.

groups.behavior: Actor coordinates, motion duration and cleanup
groups.benefit: Update the movement adaptation and replace the reconstructed planar update as matching C arrives.
groups.preserve: Terrain height service, empty-slot suspension, signed halfwords and single-precision operation order; the host owns scheduling.

groups.behavior: Scene draw ordering and actor depth comparison
groups.benefit: Replace reconstructed queue construction/comparison/sort where it affects sprite overlap.
groups.preserve: Tie ordering, signed comparisons and explicit host record ownership. Keep the correct overlay instance of the sorting routine.

groups.behavior: Actor matrices and screen placement
groups.benefit: Improve recovered camera and actor projection used by editable scene previews.
groups.preserve: Coordinate spaces, float widths, matrix order and integrated-graphics renderer boundary. Full RSP emulation is not a prerequisite.

groups.behavior: Actor tint, material and primitive-color animation
groups.benefit: Use recovered material/color behavior when improving scene appearance.
groups.preserve: The native renderer remains responsible for drawing. Current adaptations cover the relevant CPU behavior, not every display-list operation.

groups.behavior: Combat/body image conversion and resource interpretation
groups.benefit: Sprite strides compile unchanged accepted C; the child layout and delta arithmetic use portable adaptations. Conversion/allocation and registry functions remain possible later consumers.
groups.preserve: 00203664 currently supplies delta kernels, with recursive resolution and bounded storage still host-owned. Preserve big-endian lanes, palette/opacity handling and edited child independence. RGBA32 has zero secondary bytes. The N64 allocator and reverse-argument memcpy are not PC services.

groups.behavior: Cutscene command dispatch, control flow and input substitution
groups.benefit: Track accepted-source changes against existing PC adaptations rather than re-deriving scene control flow.
groups.preserve: Explicit services, bounded suspension, word-wise substitution and missing-input errors. Stored target sources in game/director are references; the portable adaptations execute on PC.

groups.behavior: Scene service updates and resource queue scheduling
groups.benefit: Use matching control flow to clarify relevant scene service ordering without reconstructing the whole game scheduler.
groups.preserve: A matching hybrid function is useful reference but must not be labeled matching pure C. Host services and suspension stay explicit.

groups.behavior: Class artwork handles, speed and presentation
groups.benefit: Track upstream improvements to existing class-body adaptations.
groups.preserve: Intentional full-handle support and expanded tables; the original handle getter masks to 12 bits. Preserve editor extensions rather than blindly restoring retail limits.

groups.behavior: Default equipment appearance and combat-body registration
groups.benefit: Track existing appearance adaptations and assess remaining useful registration behavior.
groups.preserve: Only resolve_variant from 00207658 is adapted here; its entire pool allocator is not integrated. Retain explicit host resource lifetime and modified class visual policies.

groups.behavior: Weapon/body equipment selection and classification
groups.benefit: Replace reconstructed predicates for equipment choice and linked body classification.
groups.preserve: Expanded item limits, host bounds and primary/secondary body distinction.

groups.behavior: Animation/facing to physical pose-state lookup
groups.benefit: Refresh the recovered flat-list lookup if it becomes matching pure C.
groups.preserve: Match position is the state, not the stored value; retain signed sentinels, wrapping and bounds. An adapted hybrid reference is not an imported pure-C function.

groups.behavior: Direct-descriptor animation execution
groups.benefit: Track accepted changes to the direct-descriptor path already running through portable C.
groups.preserve: Bounded stacks, explicit byte storage and resumable host callbacks.

groups.behavior: Background/image placement, scale and rotation
groups.benefit: Replace reconstructed image transforms as matching C arrives, improving cutscene backgrounds.
groups.preserve: Current edited-image support, arithmetic widths and packed-matrix intermediates.

groups.behavior: Camera/scene transforms and completion
groups.benefit: Replace reconstructed updates; the completion predicate already adapts accepted C.
groups.preserve: Host-owned jobs and the original completion semantics.

groups.behavior: Camera projection initialization and interpolation
groups.benefit: Replace reconstructed init/update around the already adapted accepted start routine.
groups.preserve: Frame count narrowing, float order and separate coordinate spaces.

groups.behavior: Dialogue layout and draw-command generation
groups.benefit: Track updates to already integrated dialogue geometry and rendering services.
groups.preserve: Big-endian fields, bounded resource access and the explicit PC draw sink.

groups.behavior: Dialogue movement and prefix controls
groups.benefit: Replace reconstructed dialogue motion/prefix behavior when matching C becomes available.
groups.preserve: Halfword truncation, completion flags and stopping before the first body-text control.

groups.behavior: Sepia and warm color conversion
groups.benefit: Track accepted source changes against the existing portable pixel transforms.
groups.preserve: Alpha bits and exact integer rounding; PC byte order is explicit.

groups.behavior: Retail class-family lookup during ROM export
groups.benefit: Track updates to an unchanged accepted source already compiled during applicable user exports.
groups.preserve: This original function has a retail bound; expanded-family exports use the maintained extension path.

groups.behavior: Promotion compatibility mask lookup
groups.benefit: Track the accepted base of the existing configurable ROM-side reader.
groups.preserve: Relocated per-class masks and expanded class IDs.

groups.behavior: Class-change lists, navigation, discovery and equipment lists
groups.benefit: Replace or update maintained modified-game C with accepted source where it simplifies ROM rebuilding.
groups.preserve: New families and linked families, expanded rosters, empty-list protection, larger IDs and the game's eligibility/service ordering. Matching C alone does not remove retail limits.

groups.behavior: Save-editor leader restrictions and Soldier reserve groups
groups.benefit: Use recovered helpers for reserve allocation, group HP/count and fixed leaders.
groups.preserve: B81CC is a larger owner: only its new-group HP segment is currently adapted. Preserve packed-save ownership, maximum capacities and Undo.

groups.behavior: New unit base stats, growth family and equipment
groups.benefit: Use accepted initialization logic for the save editor's Add unit workflow.
groups.preserve: Levels 1–99, growth-class transitions, default/explicit equipment, retail HP/STR getter reuse and final luck reset. Preserve injected randomness, expanded IDs, bounds and atomic record changes.

groups.behavior: Scenario squad conditions, evaluation and lifecycle
groups.benefit: Assess the accepted Squad W3 batch for meaningful route/condition explanations and bounded previews of authored squad behavior.
groups.preserve: These are candidate consumers, not a claim the editor already implements this runtime. Full battle/world simulation is not required for route editing. Read each function's services before selecting a subset.

groups.behavior: Shop price, classification and menu rules
groups.benefit: The full stock producer uses accepted-derived C during export. Assess the remaining price/classification helpers when they improve an editor workflow.
groups.preserve: Current expanded shop IDs, stronghold assignments and native Qt interaction. Porting the game's complete menu renderer is not required.

groups.behavior: Save record validation, signatures, checksums and copy services
groups.benefit: Accepted-derived byte-sum and bit-count routines run in PC save editing and source-built ROM exports. Existing read, validation, copy and slot-check services follow the accepted chain with explicit host storage and expanded layouts.
groups.preserve: Retain both checksum lanes, physical-offset seeds, zero-seed Pak records, signature-first validation and cleared suspend semantics. Keep expanded records, capacity checks, unknown bytes and atomic Undo. Original DMA/allocation is supplied by the ROM runtime or host, not executed directly on the PC.

groups.behavior: Squad pursuit, targeting, turning and movement-cell evaluation
groups.benefit: Complete accepted Squad W4 source is bundled for future movement and behavior previews. Source availability does not mean the editor simulates this runtime.
groups.preserve: All 21 owners are retained together, including target reset/eligibility, turning, cell correction and cleanup. The current Routes editor edits and summarizes orders; it does not provide live squad flags, dynamic target lists, terrain cost tables or N64 object lifetimes. Adapt those inputs explicitly when adding a consumer.
